constraints: One writable goal matrix is the sole semantic authority; domain views are read-only projections.

Desktop and web use one application source tree, component set, command surface, and service contract.
The public web profile hides host-dependent controls but does not delete their implementation or internal service contracts.
Publicly addressable internal APIs require authentication, authorization, quotas, origin policy, and server-side cost controls.
Feature visibility is never treated as an authorization boundary.
Browser bundles contain no provider credentials, private keys, host paths, or secret-bearing configuration.
Models and harnesses cannot mutate matrix state, approve promotion, publish, deploy, or bypass tool policy.
LFM2-350M is a lightweight browser and bounded-task model, not the universal coding model.
Every executable subgoal has at least one atomic-action child with one owner, output, acceptance gate, and evidence path.
One atomic leaf may be claimed at a time; shared matrix and ledger writes are serialized.
Simulations are forecasts and cannot promote implementation nodes.
Final promotion, default-branch integration, deployment, credentials, payments, and external submissions remain human-controlled.
Product runtime code remains untouched during matrix setup.

authorityModel.rule: The matrix is writable authority; the ledger is append-only history; queue, capsules, domain views, catalogs, and simulations are derived or factual support artifacts.

featureStateModel.implemented: The capability exists in the shared application source.
featureStateModel.visible: The selected runtime profile presents the control.
featureStateModel.enabled: The current runtime has a usable execution path.
featureStateModel.authorized: The current actor and service session may execute it.
featureStateModel.supported: The capability is covered by the stated production support level.

apiBoundary.stability: no external compatibility or SLA promise
apiBoundary.rule: Reachability does not imply authorization, public support, or permission to consume host resources.

validationPolicy.rule: A plan, simulation, count, compile, or candidate artifact cannot prove runtime behavior.
validationPolicy.humanViewQuestion: Have I checked what the human would actually see, and do I need screenshots, visual inspection, launch-state inspection, or before/after comparison to validate this properly?

simulationPolicy.rule: Simulation identifies design gaps and expected failure behavior but never promotes implementation.

harnessPolicy.authority: NexusCentral owns runs, routing, SimSpace, tool policy, validation, artifacts, approvals, and cancellation.
harnessPolicy.toolRule: A production harness must route tool requests through the NexusCentral tool broker or prove equivalent enforcement.
harnessPolicy.stateRule: Harness sessions may emit resumable references but cannot become the canonical run or matrix authority.
